from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Ensure LaTeX cleanup doesn't interfere in some environments
        config.no_latex_cleanup = True
        
        lecture_lines = ["Let I sub n be the integral.", "We integrate sine to the power n.", "The area flattens as n increases."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Sine Power Integral", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects with proper escaping for LaTeX
        i_n_formula = MathTex(r"I_n = \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^n(x) \, dx", color=WHITE)
        reduction_formula = MathTex(r"I_n = \frac{n-1}{n} I_{n-2}", color=YELLOW)
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        self.place_at_grid(i_n_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(i_n_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # i_n_formula is a MathTex object; index 0 contains the whole LaTeX string.
        # Sub-indices usually correspond to characters if not using \splittex.
        # Selecting the 'n' in \sin^n(x)
        n_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(i_n_formula[0][8], color=RED)
        self.play(Create(n_highlight))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        self.play(FadeOut(n_highlight))
        self.place_at_grid(reduction_formula, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(reduction_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Recursive Ratio", [
            "I sub n relates to I sub n minus 2.", 
            "The ratio of integrals approaches one.", 
            "This creates our infinite sequence."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show ratio R_n = I_{n+1} / I_n
        ratio_text = MathTex(r"R_n = \frac{I_{n+1}}{I_n}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_text, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(ratio_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Demonstrate R_n approaches 1 as n grows
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["C5"], color="#00FF00")
        limit_text = MathTex(r"n \to \infty, R_n \to 1", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(limit_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the squeeze between (n/(n+1)) and 1
        # Added tex_template=TexTemplate() to handle potential LaTeX compilation issues
        squeeze = MathTex(r"\frac{n}{n+1} < R_n < 1", color="#FFA500")
        self.place_at_grid(squeeze, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(squeeze))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Substitute integrals into our ratio formula.", "Isolate pi over two through algebra.", "The beautiful Wallis product emerges.", "Each term refines our value.", "It is an infinite product."]
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Wallis Product", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects using Tex to avoid potential DVI conversion issues with MathTex
        i_even = Tex("$I_{2n} = \\frac{(2n-1)!!}{(2n)!!} \\cdot \\frac{\\pi}{2}$", color=WHITE)
        i_odd = Tex("$I_{2n+1} = \\frac{(2n)!!}{(2n+1)!!}$", color=WHITE)
        wallis = Tex("$\\frac{\\pi}{2} = \\prod_{n=1}^{\\infty} \\left( \\frac{2n}{2n-1} \\cdot \\frac{2n}{2n+1} \\right)$", color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(i_even, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(i_odd, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(i_even), Write(i_odd))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Just show algebra process logic visually
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(wallis, "C4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(wallis))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight components
        box = SurroundingRectangle(wallis, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(box))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Convergence", [
            "Partial products oscillate around pi over two.",
            "Each step narrows the gap.",
            "The value homes in exactly."
        ])
        
        # --- Elements ---
        target_val = PI / 2
        line = NumberLine(x_range=[1.2, 2.0, 0.1], length=5, include_numbers=True).rotate(90 * DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'C4')
        
        target_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(line.n2p(target_val))
        label = Text("π/2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(target_dot, RIGHT)
        
        point = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        point.move_to(line.n2p(1.3)) # Start off-target
        
        self.add(line, target_dot, label, point)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Simulate oscillation
        path = VGroup()
        current_val = 1.3
        for i in range(1, 6):
            # Oscillation logic: approaching target
            direction = 1 if i % 2 != 0 else -1
            current_val = target_val + direction * (0.5 / i)
            target_pos = line.n2p(current_val)
            self.play(point.animate.move_to(target_pos), run_time=0.5)
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Narrowing gap
        for i in range(6, 11):
            direction = 1 if i % 2 != 0 else -1
            current_val = target_val + direction * (0.2 / i)
            target_pos = line.n2p(current_val)
            self.play(point.animate.move_to(target_pos), run_time=0.4)
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Homing in
        target_pos = line.n2p(target_val)
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(target_pos).set_color(RED), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Flash(point, color=RED))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Calculus meets the circle constant pi.", "Wallis provides deep numerical insight.", "A elegant dance toward the truth."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Significance", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        wallis = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi}{2} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( \frac{4n^2}{4n^2-1} \right)", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(wallis, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(wallis))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        gaussian = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx = \sqrt{\pi}", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(gaussian, "D2", scale_factor=1.2)
        gaussian.set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(gaussian))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.play(Indicate(wallis), Indicate(gaussian))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance Toward Pi
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Sine Power Integral
sections.content: Introduce the reduction formula for the integral of sin^n(x) from 0 to π/2. Explain that as n increases, this integral value acts as a gateway to understanding the behavior of ratios of these integrals.
sections.example: Visualize a 'folding' animation where the area under sin^n(x) shrinks and flattens against the x-axis as n grows, showing the transition from a hump to a thin spike.

sections.title: The Recursive Ratio
sections.content: Establish the relationship between I_n (the integral of sin^n(x)) and I_{n-2}. Show how the ratio I_{n}/I_{n-1} approaches 1 as n goes to infinity, leading to the construction of a product sequence.
sections.example: An animated 'scales' visual where two buckets (representing the integrals) are balanced against each other, gradually adjusting weights until they stabilize at a ratio of 1.

sections.title: Deriving the Wallis Product
sections.content: Substitute the integral results into the ratio formula. Step-by-step algebraic manipulation to isolate π/2, resulting in the elegant infinite product: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7)...
sections.example: Display an infinite conveyor belt where number tiles (2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6...) drop into the numerator and (1, 3, 3, 5, 5, 7...) into the denominator, slowly assembling the value of π.

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence
sections.content: Demonstrate how the partial products of the Wallis formula oscillate above and below π/2, narrowing down the target value over time.
sections.example: A digital 'Target Practice' game where a character (e.g., a rabbit) jumps back and forth across the value π/2, with each jump becoming smaller until they land exactly on the center.

sections.title: Summary and Significance
sections.content: Recap the beauty of connecting pure calculus (integrals) to the fundamental circle constant (π). Emphasize that while slow to converge, it provides deep insight into the structure of numbers.
sections.example: A final visual showing the Wallis product emerging as a beautiful geometric pattern, connecting the algebraic equation to a perfect circle drawn on a coordinate plane.
